title: Who played what in Cuba, the homemade bass, and Willie Guitar story
summary: The lineup in Cuba is listed, including Bob Ice's improvised plywood bass. Crawford tells how bassist Willie Guitar hid stolen goods in his bass.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well who was down there with you other than Joe?

Well, let's see, Joe was playing con-hit, Briss Jones was playing clarinet, Bill Lee played tenor sax, John Chaff, the regular banjo player, played tuba, and the regular drummer, Bob McIntyre, doubled on a banjo. The bass player played a bass drum, and the piano player played a snare drum, and I was the trombone. So all in all, it worked out pretty well, you know.
Bob Ice is the bass player, he's a regular bass player.
And that's a regular bass, isn't it? Yeah. Well I call it a regular bass.

Well, I mean, we call it regular bass. No, this is a, this is a, he happened to get a few scraps of plywood, I think he got a genuine bass string, or two strings on it, he uses a couple of, what do they call these, hardware store buckles? Turnbuckles. Turnbuckles. And it produces a very effective sound, I mean, if you would close your eyes, you would swear you were listening to a genuine bass. Of course you can't look at this thing, but it sounds good.
Yeah. Very convenient too, it's got a hole cut in the side of it that he can carry all the accessories.
That's right, well, that's, I think that's how we managed to get our instruments from place to place, we just threw them right in the hole in the side of the bass, you see.
Why don't we add it, let me tell them about Willie Guitar and his bass is adoring it. Maybe you know the story better than I do, Paul.

I want to get this out. This guy Willie Guitar, who played bass and lived on Music Street, he's an old time bass man around here. I don't know, some old guys like I think Sal Mojada and Huey Hardy were talking one time to Sat, talking to me in the group and they said that Willie had a bass, had a door cut in the back of his bass, a hinged door, well concealed, and he'd go to a house party and he'd stand around and he'd see something he wanted, he'd pick out something real nice and after the party got real juiced up, nobody was paying any attention, he'd just sort of back up to whatever he wanted and open the door and stick it in there. So one night he saw a real expensive clock which had an alarm on it and he put that in there. Just as he was leaving the damn thing went off. They said he used to get a lot of stuff out of it later.
I've heard of case in a place but never bass in a place.
